audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating 6/10 and three chart rows understated a lane Renekton clearly wins early.
audit.why: 53.11% over 5131 games with the packet chart giving Renekton levels 2 through first item. I left the rating alone (it is defensible as a mechanically demanding lane) but fixed the rows.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5, Level 6 to Renekton; 2+ items to Yasuo.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was marked Skill on both layers while every prose field calls it your hardest all-in, and 2+ items was marked Renekton while the prose says Yasuo takes over.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is [Skill, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Yasuo]; whys[4]/mid describe you as nearly unkillable at 6; whys[6]/late say Shieldbow plus crit outlast your burst.
audit.corrected: Three matched pairs flipped, phases[4].why and phases[6].why restated to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup twice told you to fear Wind Wall — 'never throw Q or any skillshot into it' and a wants.foe entry claiming he Wind Walls your Q heal and poke.
audit.why: Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds'. Renekton casts no projectiles: Q is a melee AoE swing, W is point-and-click, E is a dash. Wind Wall takes nothing from you, and telling the reader to hold their combo for it costs them the trade. This is the same class of error as the Azir/Yasuo calibration case, inverted.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall only stops projectiles and you cast none — keep the combo going through it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Last Breath is called 'the clock' everywhere but its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: 70/50/30 seconds — at rank 3 it is back almost every skirmish, and it only needs any Airborne target, so a caster-minion knockup arms it.

edits.before: Dominus stats turn even fights into wins before 25 minutes. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Yasuo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Dominus soaks the Last Breath window and refills Fury for a second empowered W — almost nothing trades back into that.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Yasuo carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: Shieldbow sustain and crit DPS outlast your burst. Yasuo carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.

edits.before: This is the Renekton lane. Your kit answers his mobility directly: E closes distance, empowered W stuns him mid-dash-animation if you time the click on his body rather than his destination, and Q heals through his passive shield hits. The only thing that beats you here is his Windwall — never throw Q or any skillshot into it, and if he drops it reactively, E behind it and run the full combo through the dead zone. At level 6 Dominus soaks the Last Breath burst and lets you throw a second empowered W before the R fades; almost nothing in the game can trade back into that window.
edits.after: This is the Renekton lane. Your kit answers his mobility directly: E closes distance, empowered W is point-and-click so his dashes cannot make it whiff, and Q heals through his passive shield hits. Wind Wall stops projectiles for 4 seconds and you cast none — Q is a melee swing, W is targeted, E is a dash, so walk through it and keep the combo running. At level 6 Dominus soaks the Last Breath burst and lets you throw a second empowered W before the R fades; almost nothing in the game can trade back into that window.

edits.before: Windwall your Q heal and poke tools to drain your sustain before his all-in
edits.after: Stack Steel Tempest to two so the whirlwind knockup sets up Last Breath

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Last Breath drops to 30s at rank 3 — a stray minion knockup is enough.

edits.before: Track Yasuo's Last Breath: His all-in after a knockup. While down, you win. When it is down — W-stun + Q him.
edits.after: Last Breath needs a knockup and is only 30s at rank 3; Wind Wall blocks projectiles, and you cast none.

notes: The packet's suspectName 'His Last Breath' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Last Breath is the correct R name. The real defect was the Wind Wall advice: the page told a Renekton player to hold his combo for a wall that cannot block anything he casts. Chart edits are one atomic group of three matched pairs, all three aligning the page with the packet chart and with its own prose.
